title: Unicon primitive contract
description: How the harness and a primitive image talk, and how a primitive declares itself. The harness starts one sandboxed container from the step's image, which runs the image's own entrypoint, and mounts one directory at /work, read-write, the container's only writable place besides a small tmpfs at /tmp: inputs.json and the input files under in/ go in, and outputs.json and the output files under out/ come back when the container exits. A primitive reads the paths inputs.json names and assumes nothing else; it never sees the forge or the plan, and the network only when its declaration says network: true. The same file describes primitive.yaml, the declaration the forge compiler reads: a document is exactly one of inputs.json, outputs.json or a declaration.

inputs_file.description: inputs.json, written by the harness before the container starts. inputs for a step that runs once or for one test; batch for a primitive that takes many runs in one container.

schema_version.description: The contract version this file is written against, the one the primitive's declaration names. A primitive refuses a version it does not speak.

inputs.description: One entry per input given, keyed by the input name. An optional input the task left out is absent.

batch.description: One item per run, in the order the primitive runs them, each with the inputs for that run. Version 5 keys an item by test, version 6 by run.

test.description: Version 5: the test this item is for, <group>/<test>. outputs.json answers with the same test in the same position. The id holds a /, so a primitive that writes a file per test does not name the file after it as it is.

run.description: Version 6, in place of test: an id for this run that only the forge knows the meaning of. outputs.json answers with the same run in the same position.

outputs_file.description: outputs.json, written by the primitive before it exits. The harness checks it against this contract and against the outputs the plan declares for the step before any later step sees it. outputs for a single run, batch for a batch, one entry per item in the same order; or error alone when the primitive could not work at all. Numbers are read as the decimals they are written as.

schema_version.description: The contract version this file is written against, the same number as in inputs.json.

outputs.description: One entry per output written, keyed by the output name, outcome always among them. A file output names a path under out/, a folder output a folder under out/. On accepted every output the declaration does not mark optional is written; on any other outcome only outcome need be.

batch.description: One entry per item of inputs.json's batch, in the same order and with the same tests or runs.

error.description: Set when the primitive could not do its work at all, in one sentence for staff. The harness turns it into a system_error. A failed compile, a wrong answer or anything a contestant's program does is an outcome, never an error.

batch_key.description: What a batch item is keyed by: test in version 5, run in version 6, never both. Only version 6 carries named_files, programs and links values, and output names of the form <program>.<output>.

declaration.description: primitive.yaml, what the forge compiler reads for one version of a primitive. The repo at the forge is the name and its tag the version, so the file names neither. In the primitive's own GitHub repo the file has no image line; bootstrap writes the image by digest from the release manifest into the version it creates at the forge, so a repo's CI validates its file with a placeholder digest filled in.

title.description: A short name for the workflow editor, such as Run program. It is not the primitive's name, which is its repo, and it changes nothing that grades.

description.description: One sentence for the workflow editor saying what the primitive does. It changes nothing that grades.

schema_version.description: The contract version the primitive speaks: the schema_version of every inputs.json it is given and outputs.json it writes. 5 when left out. Only version 6 has named_files, programs and links inputs, better and bounds on a number output, outputs_from, a limit from sum or max, and cache.

image.description: The image this version runs from, by digest.

batch.description: true when the primitive takes many tests in one run, so the compiler folds a per-test step over it into one container. false when left out.

network.description: true when the container may reach the network, through the compute's proxy. false when left out: every other container has none.

cache.description: Version 6: true when the primitive reads the task's files through the machine's cache, so its step is given the cache. false when left out: the step's files are copied in.

forms.description: One to four ways to use the primitive, each named in lower case. A workflow step names none: the save picks the one form whose inputs the step gives. With forms, the ports and limits live on each form and schema_version is 6.

limits.description: The container's limits for one run, or for one item of a batch. A batch step's time_ms and cpu_ms are summed over its items; the others hold for each item.

limits_from.description: Raises a limit from a number input, so the container never dies before the primitive's own per-test limit: the limit is max(limits.<name>, input * scale + add), rounded up, where input is the number input, or the sum or the largest of one number input over the programs of a programs input.

outputs_from.description: manifest: the primitive's outputs are those listed here and also the reports of the program.yaml given on its manifest input, a file input it must declare. It reads them from what the program it runs reports, and the forge checks a step's wiring against both. programs: the outputs listed here and also, for each program its programs input gives, <name>.<output> for each output the programs port declares and <name>.<report> for each report of the program.yaml given on that program's manifest input, a file input the programs port must declare; a report is given on a verdict of 0 alone.

inputs.description: What the primitive takes, by name. Every file or folder input says whether the primitive runs what arrives there as a program.

outputs.description: What the primitive gives back, by name. outcome, of type outcome, is how a step says a test or the run did not pass, and every primitive declares it.

outcomes.description: Each outcome the step can report, with one line saying when, for the workflow editor, such as accepted: the source compiles. It changes nothing that grades.

form.description: One way to use a primitive that declares forms: its own ports and limits. The declaration's title, image and the other shared keys stay at the top.

description.description: One sentence for the workflow editor saying what this form does. It changes nothing that grades.

limit_from.description: input * scale + add, where input is one number input, or in version 6 the sum or the largest over the programs of a programs input; scale is 1 and add 0 when left out. Exactly one of input, sum and max.

input.description: The number input the limit follows.

sum.description: <port>.<input>: the sum of a number input over every program of a programs port, such as programs.memory_limit, since the programs run side by side. check_declaration.py checks that both names are declared.

max.description: <port>.<input>: the largest of a number input over every program of a programs port, such as programs.time_limit. check_declaration.py checks that both names are declared.

program_input.description: A programs port and one of its number inputs, <port>.<input>.

line.description: One line of text: not empty, not only spaces, no line break.

input_port.description: One declared input. options on an enum and nowhere else. runs on every file, folder or named_files port and nowhere else: whether the primitive runs what arrives there as a program. names on a named_files port and nowhere else: the names its files must have, when the primitive fixes them. inputs and outputs on a programs port and nowhere else. secret: the image keeps what arrives there from any program it runs from another port. optional: the port may be left without a value. description: what the port takes, for the workflow editor. A programs port, version 6, takes programs the step names, at most 8, each with the inputs the port declares, program among them, the file it runs with runs: true, which the primitive runs side by side; a links port takes the links between them. check_declaration.py allows one programs port, and a links port only beside it.

inputs.description: What each program of a programs port takes, by name, declared as the primitive's own inputs are; none of them a programs or links port.

outputs.description: What the primitive gives of each program of a programs port, by name: the output <program>.<name> for each.

names.description: The names a value must give its files, each of them; any names when left out.

description.description: One sentence for the workflow editor saying what the port takes. It changes nothing that grades.

output_port.description: One declared output. optional: the primitive may leave it out of an accepted result. better, at_least and at_most on a number and nowhere else: which way is better, and the bounds every value lies within, both inclusive; check_declaration.py also refuses an at_least above at_most. description: what the port gives back, for the workflow editor.

description.description: One sentence for the workflow editor saying what the port gives back. It changes nothing that grades.

number_meaning.description: A port that says which way is better or where its values lie.

run_id.description: One run of a version 6 batch: letters, digits, _ and -, so a primitive may name a file after it. The not refuses a trailing newline, which $ lets through in some regular expression engines.

file_name.description: A name a program sees a file under: letters, digits, _, . and -, not starting with a ., so never . or .. and never a path.

values.description: Values by port name: every output and every input of version 5.

output_values.description: Outputs by name, which in version 6 may also be <program>.<output>, from a primitive whose outputs_from is programs.

input_values.description: Inputs by port name, which in version 6 may also be named_files, programs and links values.

programs.description: A programs value, version 6: one to 8 programs, each by the name the step gives it, with its own inputs, those its port declares. The name is what links and the outputs <name>.<output> call it, and never wall_clock, which stopped_by says for the wall clock.

links.description: A links value, version 6: the pipes between the programs of the programs value beside it, each "<from> -> <to>", what the first writes read by the second. A program's first link each way is its standard output or input, and each further one a named pipe in its folder, to_<name> or from_<name>.

program_name.description: A program's name in a programs value: a port name of at most 64 characters, never wall_clock. The not refuses a trailing newline, as the name becomes a path.

value.description: One input or output value. Text, a number and a boolean are carried as themselves; a file or a folder is an object naming its path.

named_files.description: A named_files value, version 6: files by the names the program sees them under, each a file under in/ or out/.

file.description: A file in the working directory, by a path relative to /work: under in/ for an input, under out/ for an output, with no empty, . or .. segment.

folder.description: A folder in the working directory, by a path relative to /work, the tree under it with its layout.
